== Audience
You want to learn more about how to use the `ordered` library from your app, library or script.

== Introduction
`ordered` provides sets and maps that preserve insertion order.

== History

* 2011 https://github.com/amalloy[Alan Malloy] publishes the first release `ordered/ordered` to https://clojars.org/ordered/versions/0.3.0[Clojars].
It is described as "Pure-clojure implementation of ruby's ordered hash and set types".
* 2012 The library gets a new name and a new home.
Alan's `ordered` github repo gets duplicated to `flatland/ordered`.
https://github.com/flatland[Flatland] was created by https://www.geni.com/[Geni] to host their open-source works.
The first release of `org.flatland/ordered` is published to https://clojars.org/org.flatland/ordered/versions/1.4.0[Clojars].
* 2018 Alan's original GitHub repository (`amalloy/ordered`) is transferred to https://github.com/clj-commons/ordered[clj-commons/ordered] for continued maintenance and care.
We continue to publish releases to `org.flatland/ordered` maven coordinates.
Our first release was https://clojars.org/org.flatland/ordered/versions/1.5.7[v1.5.7].
We are now the canonical repository for `ordered`.

=== Babashka
`ordered` is a babashka built-in library.
There is no project setup.

== Supported Envs

For usage from Clojure on the JVM we support:

* JDK 11+ (Clojure 1.13 requires JDK 17+)
* Clojure v1.10.3 and above

For ClojureScript, we support the current release of ClojureScript.

We test on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

== Sets

[source, clojure]
----
(require '[flatland.ordered.set :as oset])

(oset/ordered-set 4 3 1 8 2)
=> #ordered/set (4 3 1 8 2)

(conj (oset/ordered-set 9 10) 1 2 3)
=> #ordered/set (9 10 1 2 3)

(into (oset/ordered-set) [7 6 1 5 6])
=> #ordered/set (7 6 1 5)

(disj (oset/ordered-set 8 1 7 2 6) 7)
=> #ordered/set (8 1 2 6)

;; Adding an element already in an ordered set does not change its
;; position in the order.
(conj (oset/ordered-set 4 3 1 8 2) 8)
=> #ordered/set (4 3 1 8 2)

;; Removing an element, then adding it back in, puts it at the end,
;; just as it would if it were never part of the set.
(-> (oset/ordered-set 4 3 1 8 2) (disj 8) (conj 8))
=> #ordered/set (4 3 1 2 8)
----

== Maps

[source, clojure]
----
(require '[flatland.ordered.map :as omap])

(omap/ordered-map :b 2 :a 1 :d 4)
=> #ordered/map ([:b 2] [:a 1] [:d 4])

(assoc (omap/ordered-map :b 2 :a 1 :d 4) :c 3)
=> #ordered/map ([:b 2] [:a 1] [:d 4] [:c 3])

(into (omap/ordered-map) [[:c 3] [:a 1] [:d 4]])
=> #ordered/map ([:c 3] [:a 1] [:d 4])

(dissoc (omap/ordered-map :c 3 :a 1 :d 4) :a)
=> #ordered/map ([:c 3] [:d 4])

;; Adding a key already in an ordered map does not change its position
;; in the order.
(assoc (omap/ordered-map :b 2 :a 1 :d 4) :b 7)
=> #ordered/map ([:b 7] [:a 1] [:d 4])

;; Removing a key, then adding it back in, puts it at the end, just as
;; it would if it were never part of the map.
(-> (omap/ordered-map :b 2 :a 1 :d 4) (dissoc :b) (assoc :b 7))
=> #ordered/map ([:a 1] [:d 4] [:b 7])
----

== ClojureScript

Both `flatland.ordered.map` and `flatland.ordered.set` work in ClojureScript.
`#ordered/map` and `#ordered/set` literals are supported in ClojureScript source at compile time.

To read these literals at runtime, you must register the tags:

[source, clojure]
----
(require '[cljs.reader :as reader]
         '[flatland.ordered.map :as omap]
         '[flatland.ordered.set :as oset])

;; we get reader errors if tags are not registered for runtime usage:
(reader/read-string "#ordered/map ([:b 1] [:a 2])")
=> ... No reader function for tag ordered/map.
(reader/read-string "#ordered/set (4 3 2)")
=> ... No reader function for tag ordered/set.

;; but if we register our tags first...
(reader/register-tag-parser! 'ordered/map omap/ordered-map)
(reader/register-tag-parser! 'ordered/set oset/into-ordered-set)

;; ... then we are fine:
(reader/read-string "#ordered/map ([:b 1] [:a 2])")
=> #ordered/map ([:b 1] [:a 2])
(reader/read-string "#ordered/set (4 3 2)")
=> #ordered/set (4 3 2)
----

A few things are JVM-only:

* `transient` support
* `flatland.ordered.common/compact`

On ClojureScript, `disj` on an `ordered-set` is O(n) rather than O(1).
